title: Chapter 3 – The Cellular Level of Organization
notes: Plasma membrane: fluid mosaic of phospholipids, proteins, cholesterol.
Integral (transmembrane) vs peripheral proteins with diverse functions.
Membrane fluidity increases with unsaturated fatty acids; cholesterol modulates fluidity.
Selective permeability: small nonpolar molecules diffuse; others need transporters.
Gradients across membrane: chemical + electrical = electrochemical gradient.
Passive transport: simple diffusion, facilitated diffusion (channels/carriers), osmosis.
Channel-mediated diffusion is ion-specific; gates control opening.
Osmosis: water moves down water potential via aquaporins and bilayer.
Tonicity: isotonic (no net change), hypotonic (cell swells), hypertonic (cell shrinks).
Active transport: primary (ATP-driven pumps) and secondary (coupled gradients).
Vesicular transport: endocytosis (receptor-mediated, phagocytosis, pinocytosis), exocytosis, transcytosis.
Cytoskeleton: microfilaments, intermediate filaments, microtubules—structure and transport.
Organelles: ER (rough/smooth), Golgi, lysosomes, peroxisomes, proteasomes, mitochondria.
Mitochondria: ATP production; own DNA; maternal inheritance.
Nucleus houses DNA; nucleolus makes rRNA; chromatin organizes genes.
Gene expression: transcription (nucleus) → translation (ribosomes).
mRNA codons, tRNA anticodons; ribosomal sites A, P, E.
DNA replication precedes cell division; semiconservative mechanism.
Cell cycle: interphase (G1, S, G2), mitosis (PMAT), cytokinesis.
Mitosis outcome: two identical diploid cells; meiosis produces haploid gametes.
Apoptosis is programmed cell death; contrasts with necrosis.
Cholesterol stabilizes membranes and reduces permeability.
Carrier-mediated diffusion shows saturation kinetics and specificity.
Primary active transport example: Na+/K+ ATPase.
Receptor-mediated endocytosis uses clathrin-coated pits.
Lysosomes digest worn organelles (autophagy) and can trigger autolysis.
Alternative splicing yields multiple proteins from one gene.
Checkpoints regulate the cell cycle; failures can lead to cancer.
Meiosis I separates homologs; Meiosis II separates sister chromatids.
Proteasomes degrade ubiquitin-tagged proteins.
